title: Shift ledger: on-call retrospective and SLO check (Nov 26-28 2028)
content:
Context: Quick internal ledger capturing the three shifts covering Nov 26–28 (PST) — oncall handoffs, the incidents we observed, short remediation, SLO snapshot, and concrete follow-ups. This is a working note; aim is to capture decisions and owners before formal postmortem is filed.
Summary headline:
- Two related on-call events: a routing/autoscaler cascade that surfaced increased 5xx and elevated tail latency for hosted API routes; and an unrelated infra maintenance causing transient instance reboots in a single Dedicated pool. Both were short-lived but produced measurable SLO impact.
Incident A: "routing cascade" (started 2028-11-26 22:18 UTC, mitigated 2028-11-27 01:05 UTC)
- Symptoms: sudden spike in 5xx (~3.8% error rate on /v1/generate for ~2.5 hours), p99 latency increase to ~780ms (SLO target: p99 < 300ms), queues filling on edge proxies for certain model routes.
- Root cause (initial): autoscaler reactive policy + recently deployed predictive-scaling feature mis-estimating warm pool sizes for multimodel requests. When several large-context requests hit, predictive scaler collapsed warm pool sizes in one AZ; router fallback tried routing to other AZs and model-variant fallbacks, which triggered cache misses and an extra layer of cold starts.
- Immediate mitigation (Nov 26–27): 1) scaled up dedicated warm pool for affected model group (+30% for 2 AZs) via runtime toggle; 2) disabled predictive-scaling flag for the group (feature flag: predictiveScalingForMultimodel=false); 3) applied short-term routing policy to prefer local AZ (avoid cross-AZ hot-paths). Error rate and p99 returned closer to baseline after these actions.
- Observed impact: ~2.1% error-budget burn for hosted API for the week window; customer-facing pages showed degraded responses for 17 minutes during peak traffic. No data-exfiltration or auth issues.
- Notes: this event exposed a gap in predictive-scaling testing for mixed-sequence-length workloads.
Incident B: Dedicated pool instance churn (2028-11-27 04:40 UTC, resolved 2028-11-27 05:10 UTC)
- Symptoms: automatic node reboots in dedicated-gpu-pool-5, resulting in 10% capacity dip for ~30 minutes. Autoscale reacted but ~5 minutes lag produced transient throttling on reserved throughput routes.
- Root cause (initial): kernel upgrade cron ran earlier that day on a subset of nodes and a kernel bug triggered reboots when combined with a specific NVIDIA driver minor version. Maintenance window overlap with a canary rolling update; cron & canary scheduling race.
- Mitigation: rolled back the canary to previous node image and drained/cordoned 3 affected nodes, applied a hotpatch kernel package (hotpatch id: KP-2028-11-27-07) then rebalanced capacity.
- Impact: no hosted API customers affected; dedicated customers experienced degraded throughput for 12–20 minutes depending on reserved ingress patterns.
SLO snapshot and telemetry notes (end of day 2028-11-28):
- Hosted API: p99 latency target 300ms; week window observed p99 = 362ms (7-day trend shows a 4% drift upward vs prior week). Error rate averaged 0.6% but spiked to 3.8% during Incident A.
- Dedicated: 99.9% availability SLA target; observed availability for dedicated pools this week = 99.92% (marginally within target but trending down for the region with kernel churn).
- Error budget: Hosted API has ~8% of weekly error budget remaining after the events (burn rate elevated). Recommend conservative routing until corrective work reduces variance.
Handoff notes (what incoming oncall needs to know):
- Current toggles: predictiveScalingForMultimodel=false applied to model-group alpha-3; do not re-enable without approval from Arjun. Toggle info in runtime config (see linked PR).
- Warm pool: warm pool for alpha-3 increased by 30% until 2028-12-04; autoscale policy will revert unless a follow-up ticket extends it.
- Dedicated pool 5: nodes rebalanced, but watch for kernel reboots; preference: keep canary image pinned to image rev v2028-11-19 until kernel bug tracked down fully.
- Contacts: primary oncall (this shift) = Maya Chen; secondary = Arjun Patel; infra lead for kernel issues = Lena Morales.
Decisions made in-shift:
- Disable predictive-scaling for multimodel by default until a regression test that simulates mixed-length bursts is added to the CI harness. (Owner: Arjun, ticket SRE-1423)
- Add a short-term rule in routing to prefer intra-AZ routing for hot model groups to reduce cross-AZ cold cache thrash; evaluate cost impact by Dec 6. (Owner: Eric Zhao)
- Pin dedicated canary image until kernel patch validated in staging. (Owner: Lena Morales)
Action items / follow-ups (concrete, with owners and target dates):
- SRE-1423: Add integration test for predictive scaler with mixed sequence lengths + golden traffic replay (Owner: Arjun Patel, due 2028-12-08).
- PR 889: runtime change to make predictive scaling opt-in per model group; finish review and merge, add rollout playbook (Owner: Maya Chen, due 2028-11-30). Linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/889
- Infra-ker-11: Investigate kernel-driver interaction and coordinate with cloud provider for stable kernel build; produce postmortem note (Owner: Lena Morales, due 2028-12-05).
- Observability: add a derived metric for "predictive-scaler-induced-coldstart-count" and an alert threshold (Owner: Monitoring team, contact Eric, due 2028-12-04).
- Customer comms: draft a short note for affected Dedicated customers with timeline and mitigation summary (Owner: Customer Success lead; suggested draft owner: Maya Chen, due 2028-11-30).
Open questions / uncertainties:
- Was there any traffic pattern (client SDK version, heavy context users) that pushed predictive scaler into a bad state? Need to cross-ref request traces with SDK versions. (Investigation ticket created: SRE-1430)
- Are there other model groups using predictive-scaling with similar characteristics? Inventory check pending (Owner: Product-Optimize, due 2028-12-06).
Quick win checklist (things we want done this sprint):
- Merge PR 889 and add rollout gating for model-groups.
- Add alert for p99-latency > 450ms for more than 10 minutes on hosted-api critical routes.
- Pin canary image for dedicated pools and delay auto-kernel upgrades until validation window complete.
Post-shift micro-retrospective (what went well / what to improve):
- Went well: Oncall team coordinated quickly (clear owner, quick toggles) and mitigations were effective within ~2.5 hours; routing fallback logic prevented a broader outage.
- To improve: predictive-scaling changes landed without a realistic mixed-workload smoke test; need guardrails (feature flag defaults and CI coverage). Observability gap: no dedicated metric to show predictive-scaler coldstart contribution.
Appendix (raw timestamps and short timeline):
- 2028-11-26 22:18 UTC — first elevated 5xx alert (edge-proxy-alert-5xx-high)
- 2028-11-26 22:27 UTC — p99 crosses 500ms; routing team paged
- 2028-11-26 22:35 UTC — predictive-scaling flag identified as possible cause; mitigation plan drafted
- 2028-11-26 23:02 UTC — warm pool increase + predictiveScalingForMultimodel=false toggled
- 2028-11-27 01:05 UTC — metrics back near baseline, incident downgraded to page notes
- 2028-11-27 04:40 UTC — dedicated pool node reboots start (kernel cron overlap)
- 2028-11-27 05:10 UTC — nodes cordoned, hotpatch applied, capacity restored

If you are taking next shift: review SLO dashboards for p99 latency and error rate for hosted routes, verify predictive-scaling toggle status, and keep an eye on dedicated pool kernel telemetry. If anything suspicious, escalate to infra lead (Lena) and flag SRE-1423 with notes.
Notes-to-self / scratch ideas: consider a nightly smoke-run that replays a small sample of real traffic patterns (mix of short/long contexts) against predictive-scaler to detect regressions early. Also propose a runbook section for "predictive-scaler anomalies" with clear rollback steps.

End of ledger.
